subject: journey/nautilus
prompt: Use case: illustration-story. A single landscape 3:2 illustration for the historical atlas sketchbook of Jules Verne's Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea. A nineteenth-century naturalist's field sketch in graphite and sepia pen with restrained transparent watercolour washes on warm ivory paper. Fine irregular parallel hatching, economical contour lines, a few details sharply observed; leave areas of cream paper around irregular unfinished edges. One coherent scene that reads at small sizes. No captions, labels, border, binding, signatures, photorealism, modern equipment, or Disney submarine designs. A barefoot Cretan free diver with dark hair in simple waistcloth swims toward the broad observation glass of the Nautilus, raising his open hand in greeting. From the dim saloon, dark rim of the window in foreground, figure fully submerged in blue-green Aegean water. No helmet or air tanks.
